KPI Definition: No. of people directly impacted (cumulative to date) - Count only people who used your solution and achieved the intended outcome. Do not include those who only signed up or were reached.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Examples
Education: 500 students served → 320 improved scores ≥15% → Report 320
Agriculture: 200 farmers served → 120 exceeded regional yield → Report 120
Financial inclusion: 1,000 accounts opened → 650 active for 3 months → Report 650

KPI Definition: No. of people indirectly impacted (cumulative to date) - Count people who did not directly use your solution, but benefited because your solution influenced systems, supply chains, institutions, communities, or policies since inception.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Examples
Education: 50 teachers trained → each teacher teaches 200 students → Report 10,000
Agriculture: 120 farmers supported → produce reaches ~300 consumers per farmer → Report 36,000
Policy / systems change: Solution adopted by 1 public agency serving ~500,000 people → Report 500,000

KPI Definition: No. of direct jobs created (cumulative to date) - Count people who are directly employed and paid by your startup as a result of building, delivering, or operating your solution.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Count only people who:
- Are on your payroll or paid as recurring contractors
- Were hired because the startup exists

Examples
Startup employs:
4 full-time staff
2 part-time staff
1 long-term contract developer
→ Report 7 direct jobs

KPI Definition: No. of indirect jobs supported or enabled (cumulative to date) - number of people who are not employed by your startup, but gain sustained employment or income opportunities because your solution expanded economic activity.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Count only people whose jobs or income exist because of your solution.

Examples
Agriculture
120 farmers adopt your solution
Each farmer hires 2 additional farm worker due to increased productivity
→ Report 240 indirect jobs

Manufacturing / Supply Chain
Startup onboards 5 small manufacturers as suppliers
Each supplier hires 3 new workers to meet demand
→ 5 × 3 = Report 15 indirect jobs

KPI Definition: CO₂ emissions saved or avoided (cumulative to date, in kg CO₂e)
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
Baseline emissions (kg CO₂e) − Emissions after using your solution (kg CO₂e)
× number of users / uses / units
= Total kg CO₂e saved or avoided

Example:
Old process = 10 kg CO₂e per use
New process = 6 kg CO₂e per use
1,000 uses
→ (10 − 6) × 1,000 = 4,000 kg CO₂e

KPI Definition: Water saved or pollution prevented (cumulative to date, in kg)
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
Baseline water use (per unit) − After using your solution (per unit)
× number of uses = Total water saved or pollution prevented (kg)

Example (pollution):
1.5 kg wastewater pollutants prevented per factory
40 factories using solution
→ 60 kg pollution prevented

KPI Definition: Waste diverted or recycled (cumulative to date, in kg)
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
Waste previously sent to landfill (kg) − Waste sent to landfill after solution (kg)
= Total waste diverted or recycled (kg)

Example:
500 kg waste generated per month
350 kg recycled using your solution
Over 12 months
→ 350 × 12 = 4,200 kg waste diverted

KPI Definition: Energy produced or shifted to renewables (cumulative to date, in kWh)
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
Renewable energy produced or shifted per unit (kWh) × number of users / systems / installations
= Total renewable energy (kWh)

Example:
500 kWh/month shifted from diesel to solar
Over 18 months
→ 9,000 kWh shifted to renewables

KPI Definition: Land or ecosystems restored or protected (cumulative to date, in hectares or m²)
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
Area restored or protected per site (ha or m²) × number of sites
= Total land or ecosystems restored/protected

Example:
2 hectares restored per site
15 sites completed
→ 30 hectares restored

KPI Definition: Grants raised after becoming a finalist - State whether your startup has received any grants after becoming a finalist. If yes, report the total grant amount received (USD) to date.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Example
Received USD 100,000 government grant after finalist announcement
→ Report: Yes, USD 100,000

KPI Definition: VC or angel funding raised after becoming a finalist - State whether your startup has raised any VC or angel funding after becoming a finalist. If yes, report the total amount (USD) raised to date.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Example
Raised USD 1.2 million in seed funding after finalist selection
→ Report: Yes, USD 1,200,000

KPI Definition: Estimated potential ROI - Estimate the potential return multiple an investor could achieve if your startup reaches a realistic exit. Report a single ROI multiple (e.g. 3×, 5×, 10×).
Calculation Method & Examples:
Example 1 — Valuation-based
Current valuation: RM5 million
Expected exit valuation: RM40 million
40 ÷ 5 = 8×
→ Report: 8×

Example 2 — Capital-based (early-stage teams)
Total capital raised to date: RM2 million
Expected exit valuation: RM12 million
12 ÷ 2 = 6×
→ Report: 6×

KPI Definition: % Revenue from top 3 customers
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
(Latest Annual Revenue from customers A/B/C ÷ total revenue) × 100

Example:
Customer A: 40%
Customer B: 20%
Customer C: 10%

KPI Definition: If no revenue, does the startup have traction in terms of dollar (USD) form of LOI/MOU?
Calculation Method & Examples: Not Specified

KPI Definition: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) - The average cost to acquire one paying customer.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
Total sales & marketing spend ÷ number of new paying customers acquired

Example:
USD 20,000 spent to acquire 10 customers

KPI Definition: Customer churn rate (%) - Report the percentage of customers lost over a year.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
(Customers lost in a year ÷ customers at start of the year) × 100

Example:
Customers at start of year: 50
Customers lost during the year: 2
→ (2 ÷ 50) × 100 = 4% annual churn

KPI Definition: Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) - Report your current recurring revenue per month from subscriptions or recurring contracts.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
Recurring monthly revenue per customer × number of active customers = MRR

Example:
10 customers paying USD 500/month → USD 5,000 MRR

KPI Definition: Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) - calculated based on recurring revenue contracts.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation:
Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) × 12 = ARR

Example:
USD 5,000 MRR → 5,000 × 12 → USD 60,000 ARR

KPI Definition: Startup Valuation
Calculation Method & Examples:
Investment-based valuation 
If you have raised equity funding:
Post-money valuation = Amount invested ÷ % equity sold

Example:
USD1,000,000 invested for 20% equity
→ 1,000,000 ÷ 0.20 = USD 5,000,000 post-money valuation

Report: USD 5,000,000 (post-money)

KPI Definition: Cash runway (months) - Estimate how many months your startup can continue operating with its current cash balance, assuming current spending levels.
Calculation Method & Examples:
Calculation: 
Runway (months) = Current cash balance ÷ Average monthly burn

Example:
Cash balance: USD 300,000
Monthly burn: USD 50,000
→ 300,000 ÷ 50,000 = 6 months runway
